content: The WHO NCD Country Capacity Survey (CCS) serves as the primary tool for tracking global progress in implementing policies related to non-communicable diseases (NCDs). This survey is conducted biennially and includes specific questions about population surveillance systems for physical activity across all age groups, as outlined in the WHO guidelines on physical activity and sedentary behavior. Since 2019, the survey has also assessed the existence of national physical activity guidelines. WHO Member States are required to provide supporting documentation for their responses. In 2019, 40% (78 out of 194) of WHO Member States reported having national physical activity guidelines. A detailed analysis of these responses revealed that only two-thirds (52 out of 78) of these countries included recommendations on the amount of physical activity their populations should engage in. Furthermore, only 42 countries fully aligned their guidelines with the 2010 WHO Global Recommendations on Physical Activity for Health. Data from the 2021 and subsequent surveys will provide insights into the adoption of updated guidelines.
